I've been mulling over some of the things about bicycles that I find counter-intuitive, so I thought I might as well list a few of them here, just for fun.

  • To turn right, you first must turn the front wheel left; to turn left, you first must turn the front wheel right (it's called counter-steering).
  • On bikes with rim brakes, the brake is mounted in front of the front fork, but behind the chainstays.
  • On bikes with disk brakes, the front brake is mounted behind the front fork, but in front of the chainstays.
  • The front derailleur has its resting (non-tensioned) position in close to the bike, but the rear derailleur has its resting position away from the bike.
  • On the front shifter, the big level shifts up the gears and the small lever shifts down; on the rear shifter, the big lever shifts down the gears, and the small lever shifts up.
  • On the rear derailleur, the biggest cog is the lowest, slowest gear and the littlist cog is the highest, fastest gear; but the opposite is true of the front derailleur.
  • To tighten a cable with the barrel adjuster, you loosen the barrel adjuster; to loosen the cable, you tighten the barrel adjuster.
  • The right pedal screws in clockwise, but the left pedal screws in counterclockwise.
  • Fat, padded saddles are actually less comfortable in the long run than skinny, unpadded saddles.
  • Fatter tires (say, 28 mm) are actually faster than skinny tires (say, 23 mm).
